Adversarially verify this code-review finding from the M12 diff. Read the actual code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default to isReal=false if it's a false positive, pre-existing, out of scope, or already handled.

Lens: a11y
Severity: low
File: app/(customer)/account/settings/page.tsx (Settings Card rows, lines ~32-64 (Email / Payment method / Notifications / Language))
Title: Label/value setting rows use unassociated spans instead of a description list
Detail: Each settings row is two sibling <span>s — a bold label (Email, Payment method, Language) and a value — with no programmatic association between them. A screen reader reads them as adjacent inline text with no name/value relationship, and the pairing isn't conveyed semantically. These are textbook definition pairs that should be marked up as such.
Suggestion: Wrap the rows in a <dl> with <dt> for each label and <dd> for each value (the StatusBadge can live inside the <dd>). This conveys the label/value relationship to assistive tech without changing the visual layout.

Let me confirm the rows are genuinely just sibling spans with no semantic association (no `aria-label`, no role) and check whether axe would catch this (it wouldn't — axe doesn't flag missing `<dl>`, so the passing axe test does not refute the finding).

The code at lines 38-67 confirms: each row is a `<div>` containing two sibling `<span>`s (or a span + StatusBadge), with no `id`/`aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` linkage, no `role`, nothing tying label to value. A screen reader reads them as adjacent inline text.

Let me do one adversarial check: is there any wrapping mechanism or visually-hidden association I might be missing, and is the "Notifications" row even a true definition pair (the suggestion says StatusBadge can live in `<dd>`).

The only `aria-*` attributes are `aria-hidden="true"` on decorative icons. There is no programmatic label/value association whatsoever. The rows are confirmed to be sibling `<span>`s (label) + `<span>`/`StatusBadge` (value) inside a flex `<div>`, exactly as the finding describes.

My adversarial verification conclusion:

**Attempts to refute, all failed:**
1. **Pre-existing?** No — the file is added (`A`) in M12; all four rows are added lines.
2. **False positive on the markup claim?** No — confirmed two sibling spans per row, no `id`/`aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby`/`role`, no visually-hidden association. Decorative icons are correctly `aria-hidden`, but that doesn't create a label/value relationship.
3. **Already handled by passing axe tests?** No — axe does not flag the absence of `<dl>` markup for label/value pairs, so the green axe test on this screen does not cover or refute this issue.
4. **Out of scope / against convention?** The opposite — the project already uses `<dl>/<dt>/<dd>` for the same label/value pattern in `app/(customer)/session/[id]/summary/page.tsx` and `components/admin/ProviderApprovalCard.tsx`. This new screen diverges from an established convention.

The finding is accurate and consistent with the codebase's own conventions. Severity "low" is appropriate: the content is still readable by screen readers as adjacent text, just without the semantic name/value pairing — a minor enhancement, not a blocker.
